newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: cricket - England cricketers pull in the punters.
newsitem.headline: cricket - England cricketers pull in the punters.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Jan 30 - England might be struggling with their test match and one-day international record but they have inspired New Zealand cricket fans in a way not seen since the 1992 World Cup, NZPA reports.
New Zealand Cricket (NZC) chief executive Christopher Doig said yesterday sales for the forthcoming five-match one-day series were "streets ahead of anything since the World Cup".
"The test match bookings are modest, but even then we never usually have any pre-bookings for them. So merely having some already is a sign of interest.
"But the opening one-day international scheduled for Lancaster Park (Christchurch, February 20), the ground's first day-night international, is already half sold.
"The Basin Reserve is always well booked while Napier, for another day-nighter, is pretty good," Doig said.
"The two games to be played at Eden Park are outstanding. Several thousand tickets for both have already been sold," he added.
Doig said the demand for tickets reflected a positive view of New Zealand cricket at the moment.
"People also realise New Zealand is in with a chance. England is quality opposition no matter what its recent record is and certainly from a marketing perspective it is seen as credible opposition."
